task_brief: This is day 8 of "Arts, Culture, and Context". That is unit 5 in grade 4. Today is a varied re-practice about community traditions. It takes about 40–60 minutes. It is one day's work, not the whole unit project. Your unit is working toward this: Curate a small context-rich exhibit or playlist using permitted images, audio, descriptions, or learner-created work. Today helps by working on community traditions. Your unit also covers art as communication, community traditions, artist context, and respectful cultural learning. Today is for practice. You are scored on finishing and being honest, not on getting it perfect.
primary_task: Try community traditions again in a different way. If you drew it before, write it this time. If you listened before, put it on paper this time. Make three short studies. Spread them out over the session. After each, write what this new way helped you see. This is not for a grade. It checks that you understand community traditions in more than one way. Keep it private. Keep today's work tied to your unit. Today is about community traditions. It is part of "Arts, Culture, and Context". Later days in this unit cover other things, like art as communication. Before you stop, do this check: In one concise response, show or explain the most important idea about community traditions; then identify one check that would catch an error or weak claim. In grade 4, try the steps yourself before you ask for help. Give a reason in your own words for at least one choice. A labelled drawing or a spoken answer counts fully.

presentation_and_privacy.presentation_options: You choose the audience. Keeping the work entirely to yourself, showing it to one parent or trusted adult, or submitting it as a file with no one watching are all full-credit options. No public performance, exhibition, class presentation, live audience, photograph, camera, or voice recording is required at any point in this task, and choosing the most private option never lowers the score.
presentation_and_privacy.text_or_no_audio_alternative: A written alternative is always available and scores the same. Instead of performing, speaking, or recording, you may submit a written description of what you made or would make, a notated or diagrammed version, a labelled plan, or a written analysis covering the same criteria. Nothing in this task requires a working microphone, camera, or the ability to perform aloud.

copyright_and_authorship: The graded submission must be your own authorship. A parent, tutor, or AI tool may explain an idea, demonstrate a technique, or give feedback on a draft, but must not produce, write, debug, or make any part of the work that is scored. Any material you did not create yourself must be in the public domain, openly licensed, or used as a short cited excerpt for study — reproduce no more than the point requires, credit the maker and the source, and never copy full lyrics, a complete score, or a whole image and present it as your own.
accessibility_options: Provide readable text plus optional audio or read-aloud support; no voice feature is required.
Chunk directions into one action at a time and show a worked example or model.
Allow typed, handwritten, spoken, drawn, manipulatives-based, or demonstrated responses when the standard permits.
Offer reduced-copying, extended-time, hidden-timer, movement-break, and low-distraction options.
Use captions, alt text, high-contrast print, keyboard access, and text-only fallbacks for media.
Preserve the learning target while adjusting quantity, pacing, representation, or response mode.
task_accessibility_provisions: You can take a break, stretch, or come back to this later. That does not lower your score.
safety_and_privacy_rules: Allow a pause, break, or alternate response mode without treating it as failure.
Protect hearing, ventilation, tool safety, copyright, cultural context, and respectful representation.
No public performance, voice recording, photo, or camera use is ever required; provide a private, written, or no-audio alternative for every task.
Use only original student work, public-domain material, or properly licensed excerpts; never reproduce full copyrighted lyrics, sheet music, or protected works.
The final product must remain the student’s own authorship; adult or AI assistance may support planning and feedback but must not create the graded work.

media.suggestion: Optional diagram, map, worked example, source image, demonstration, or short clip supporting community traditions.
media.fallback: Provide the same information as readable steps, alt text, transcript, tactile/concrete model, or teacher demonstration.

remediation: Reteaching for community traditions follows the signal actually observed, not a fixed script. If the signal is "prerequisite gap": Return to the smallest prerequisite needed for community traditions, model it with a concrete or text-only representation, then retry one fresh item. If the signal is "procedure without understanding": Ask the learner to explain or represent why the process for community traditions works before continuing. If the signal is "correct but low confidence": Confirm the reasoning specifically, offer one varied example of community traditions, and avoid unnecessary remediation. If the signal is "repeated error pattern": Name the observable pattern neutrally, contrast it with a worked example, and schedule a short same-day or next-session review. If the signal is "mastery evidence": Require accurate independent application plus explanation on a later or different occasion before marking community traditions mastered. Re-check with one fresh item of the same kind before moving on, and record which signal was seen so the pattern is visible across the unit rather than treated as a one-off.
extension: Apply community traditions under a new constraint, compare two approaches or perspectives, or teach the idea with an original example without completing another learner’s graded work. Treat this as optional depth on community traditions rather than extra volume: one harder case done well beats three more of the same. Extension work stays private by default and uses only original, public-domain, or properly cited material. Extension work is never required to reach mastery and must not be assigned as a penalty.
